findings.evidence: KeePass must be downloaded and installed
findings.rationale: Uses passive voice without specifying who performs the download and installation, and omits target platform, version, or source preconditions.

findings.evidence: has no limits in length. A whole sentence can be used with more than 100 characters.
findings.rationale: Uses illustrative weak phrasing ('can be used') and leaves unclear whether 'no limits in length' permits an empty (0-character) password.

findings.evidence: Folder selected must be of type the database can read and that is “name”.kdb
findings.rationale: Conflates a 'Folder' with a .kdb file, uses unclear syntax ('type the database can read', 'and that is'), and leaves unclear whether '“name”.kdb' denotes any filename with a .kdb extension or a literal name.

findings.evidence: Folder selected must be of type the database can read
findings.rationale: Does not specify who selects the target or how the system handles selection of an unsupported or unreadable file.

findings.evidence: Databases must have different names or else the previews one will be replace if selected
findings.rationale: Contains unclear referents ('the previews [previous] one', 'if selected'—for creation, saving, or opening?) and does not define uniqueness scope (same directory vs. globally, case sensitivity).

findings.evidence: the previews one will be replace if selected
findings.rationale: Fails to specify the directory/scope of name uniqueness and whether user confirmation or a warning is required before overwriting an existing database.

findings.evidence: There must be entries in the database in order for them to be printed
findings.rationale: Unclear whether 'them' refers to all entries in the database or only selected/filtered entries, and whether plural 'entries' requires more than one entry.

findings.evidence: There must be entries in the database in order for them to be printed
findings.rationale: Does not specify system behavior (e.g., disabled print option or error message) when printing is attempted on an empty database.

findings.evidence: All data related to the word must be shown.
findings.rationale: 'All data related to the word' is vague regarding which fields are searched, matching criteria (case sensitivity, substring vs. whole word), and whether sensitive fields like passwords are shown in plaintext.

findings.evidence: All data related to the word must be shown.
findings.rationale: Omits system behavior when no entries match the search term or when the query is empty.

findings.evidence: A name is required in order for the new group/subgroup to be created
findings.rationale: Does not specify valid name rules (e.g., whitespace-only names, forbidden characters, length limits, or uniqueness).

findings.evidence: A name is required in order for the new group/subgroup to be created
findings.rationale: Does not specify the system behavior or error handling when group/subgroup creation is attempted without a name.

findings.evidence: A subgroup cannot be created when no group is selected
findings.rationale: Does not specify how the system enforces or reports this restriction (e.g., disabling the action or showing an error message).

findings.evidence: A name is required in order for the group/subgroup to be renamed
findings.rationale: Does not specify valid name constraints (e.g., whitespace-only names, character restrictions, or duplicate names).

findings.evidence: A name is required in order for the group/subgroup to be renamed
findings.rationale: Does not specify how the system responds if the user provides an empty name during renaming.

findings.evidence: In order to find something in a group a word must be placed in the find field
findings.rationale: Both 'something' (entries, subgroups, or specific fields) and 'a word' (single word vs. multi-word phrase or substring) are vague.

findings.evidence: a word must be placed in the find field
findings.rationale: Omits the actor and the system behavior when a find operation is triggered with an empty field or returns no results.

findings.evidence: An entry must belong to a group to be created
findings.rationale: Syntactically ambiguous phrasing ('a group to be created' could be misread as the group being created rather than an existing group required before creating an entry).

findings.evidence: An entry must belong to a group to be created
findings.rationale: Does not specify how the system behaves when entry creation is attempted without a selected or assigned group.

findings.evidence: When the password field is completed the repeat password field must be completed
findings.rationale: 'is completed' is vague (non-empty vs. focus loss vs. form submission) and does not specify whether this applies to entry passwords, master passwords, or both.

findings.evidence: the repeat password field must be completed
findings.rationale: Does not specify the system response when the password field is filled in but the repeat password field is left blank.

findings.evidence: Password field and repeat password field must be identical
findings.rationale: Does not clarify which password dialog (entry vs. master password) this rule applies to.

findings.evidence: Password field and repeat password field must be identical
findings.rationale: Does not specify what happens when the password and repeat password fields do not match.

findings.evidence: An entry must be selected to be viewed or modified
findings.rationale: Does not specify the system behavior (e.g., disabled controls or error message) when no entry is selected.

findings.evidence: repeat password field must be Changed and be identical with password field
findings.rationale: Does not specify what error handling occurs when the repeat password field is unchanged or mismatched, nor which form context applies.

findings.evidence: When the password field is changed the repeat password field must be Changed and be identical with password field
findings.rationale: Overlaps with and restates the repeat-password completion requirement (KP-012) and equality requirement (KP-013), substituting 'changed' for 'completed' without clarifying distinct contexts.

findings.evidence: An entry must be selected before it is duplicated
findings.rationale: Does not specify how the system behaves if duplication is invoked when no entry is selected.

findings.evidence: For the following features, use cases are not included
findings.rationale: 'the following features' has no clear referent within the requirement (leaving unclear whether it refers to KP-018 through KP-032), and 'a browser' does not specify supported browsers.

findings.evidence: An internet connection and a browser are required in order to download new language translations
findings.rationale: Does not specify what happens if no internet connection or browser is available, nor how downloaded translations are installed or activated.

findings.evidence: The prefix “Auto-Type:” is required in front of each sequence
findings.rationale: 'each sequence' has no defined referent here (its location in a note field is only mentioned later in KP-020), and it is unclear whether 'Auto-Type:' is case-sensitive or requires a following space.

findings.evidence: The prefix “Auto-Type:” is required in front of each sequence
findings.rationale: Does not specify where sequences are entered or how a sequence missing the required prefix is handled.

findings.evidence: Sequence’s length must not be more than a line (59 characters)
findings.rationale: Conflates 'a line' with a 59-character limit and leaves unclear whether the 59-character limit includes the 'Auto-Type:' prefix from KP-018.

findings.evidence: Sequence’s length must not be more than a line (59 characters)
findings.rationale: Does not specify how the system handles sequences exceeding 59 characters (e.g., error, truncation, or ignoring).

findings.evidence: If two auto-types are referred in one note field
findings.rationale: Unclear whether 'two auto-types are referred' also applies to three or more auto-type references, and what 'referred' means syntactically.

findings.evidence: only the first is used
findings.rationale: Does not specify whether additional auto-type sequences in the note field are silently ignored or produce a user warning/error.

findings.evidence: Only one database file is allowed in command line options
findings.rationale: Does not specify how the application handles multiple database file arguments passed on the command line.

findings.evidence: database file
findings.rationale: Refers to the .kdb database as a 'database file', whereas KP-003 refers to it as a 'Folder' and KP-004 refers to it as 'Databases'.

findings.evidence: In case a space is found in the path, it must be enclosed into quotes
findings.rationale: 'it' could grammatically refer to either 'a space' or 'the path', and 'quotes' does not specify single versus double quotation marks.

findings.evidence: it must be enclosed into quotes
findings.rationale: Does not specify which paths (e.g., command-line arguments) are covered or what error handling occurs if a path containing spaces is unquoted.

findings.evidence: the database doesn’t open unless the password is entered
findings.rationale: States 'unless the password is entered' without specifying that the entered password must match the valid master password.

findings.evidence: the database doesn’t open unless the password is entered
findings.rationale: Does not specify error feedback, retry behavior, or lockout rules when the password is omitted or incorrect.

findings.evidence: unless the key file is present
findings.rationale: 'is present' is vague regarding where the key file must reside or be selected and whether it must validate against the database key.

findings.evidence: the database doesn’t open unless the key file is present
findings.rationale: Does not specify the error handling or user notification when the key file is missing, unreadable, or invalid.

findings.evidence: If there is a composite key
findings.rationale: 'composite key' is never defined in the SRS, leaving unclear how it is configured or whether other credentials (such as a Windows user account) may be included.

findings.evidence: both master password and key file are required
findings.rationale: Does not specify the system behavior or error feedback when only one of the required composite-key factors is supplied.

findings.evidence: File formats are not specialized password database formats
findings.rationale: Both 'File formats' (which formats?) and 'specialized password database formats' are undefined and vague.

findings.evidence: File formats are not specialized password database formats
findings.rationale: Fails to specify which file formats this requirement applies to (e.g., database files vs. import/export formats).

findings.evidence: File formats are not specialized password database formats
findings.rationale: Conflicts with KP-003 and KP-021, which specify .kdb as a specialized database file type/format read by KeePass.

findings.evidence: File formats only specify a low-level layout of stored data
findings.rationale: Both 'File formats' and 'low-level layout' are vague, leaving unclear which formats are meant and which structural or cryptographic aspects are included.

findings.evidence: File formats only specify a low-level layout of stored data
findings.rationale: Omits which file formats are covered and what defines the high-level structure or semantics of the stored data.

findings.evidence: Global hot key cannot be changed
findings.rationale: 'Global hot key' is not defined anywhere in the SRS, leaving unclear what action it invokes and in what context it operates.

findings.evidence: Global hot key cannot be changed
findings.rationale: Does not specify the fixed key combination assigned to the global hot key.

findings.evidence: Title, username or URL cannot be changed in a TAN entry.
findings.rationale: 'TAN entry' is not defined in the SRS, and it is unclear whether other fields (such as password or notes) may be modified.

findings.evidence: Title, username or URL cannot be changed in a TAN entry.
findings.rationale: Does not specify whether these fields are disabled/read-only or rejected with an error, nor whether they can be set when initially creating the TAN entry.

findings.evidence: When a TAN is used
findings.rationale: 'used' is vague because it does not define which action marks a TAN as used (e.g., copying, Auto-Type, viewing, or manual confirmation).

findings.evidence: it expires automatically and can never be used again.
findings.rationale: Does not specify how expiration is visually indicated or enforced if a user attempts to reuse an expired TAN.
